references.text: The same command to be holy because the Lord is holy. A foundational text on holiness that is repeated in Leviticus 20:7.
Parallel command: 'You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.' The same theological basis for holiness.
Repeats the theme of holiness later in the same chapter, emphasizing that the Lord has set Israel apart from the nations.
The Lord sanctifies His people. Shows that holiness comes from God Himself.
Israel shall be a holy nation and a kingdom of priests. The basis for the call to holiness.
Israel is a holy people to the Lord. Confirms the people's special position and calling to holiness.
Peter quotes Leviticus and urges believers to be holy in all their conduct, because God is holy.
God's will is sanctification. New Testament application of the call to holiness.
Pursue holiness, for without it no one will see the Lord. Continues the theme of the necessity of holiness.
The Lord will sanctify His great name. Shows God's initiative in sanctifying His people.
